EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East is on high alert as the United States issues renewed, strong threats against Iran, with President Trump stating Iran must "move fast - otherwise nothing will be left of them." This comes amidst reports of ongoing US-Israeli coordination for potential renewed military action and a drone attack on the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, attributed by the UAE to projectiles from its "western border," though the exact origin remains under investigation.

IRAN
US President Trump issued severe warnings to Iran, stating "the clock is ticking" and they must "move fast - otherwise nothing will be left of them." He is scheduled to meet with his national security team on Tuesday to discuss military options, following a call with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu about Iran and his trip to China. Iranian sources (@asafroz, @amitsegal) reported five US conditions for a deal: no reparations, transfer of 400kg of enriched uranium, only one nuclear facility to remain active, less than 25% of frozen funds released, and ceasefire conditional on negotiations. Iran's counter-conditions include ending war on all fronts, lifting sanctions, releasing all frozen funds, war damages compensation, and recognition of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohsen Rezaei, senior advisor to Iran's Leader, warned that the "Strait of Hormuz will be closed for military deployment and insecurity." He threatened that if Iranian oil facilities are targeted, all regional oil facilities, "friend or foe," would be attacked, potentially disrupting global oil supply for a significant period. Iran's Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref stated Iran would "no longer allow the enemy's military equipment to pass through the Strait of Hormuz." Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf was appointed Special Envoy for China. Press TV claims US "Operation Epic Fury" against Iran has ended, but also reports Iran can sustain conflict for months, retaining 60% of its missile capability and 90% of 33 underground missile sites near Hormuz are operational.

ISRAEL
Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke with President Trump about Iran and China, stating Israel is "prepared for every scenario" regarding Iran and is intensifying efforts against evolving drone threats, including fiber-optic guided drones. Netanyahu confirmed the elimination of Bahaa Baroud, a Hamas operations commander, and asserted that 60% of the mission in Gaza is complete. The IDF reported a critical manpower shortage, lacking approximately 12,000 soldiers in mandatory service, including 6,000-7,500 combat soldiers, and experiencing "deep erosion" in active and reserve forces.

Four IDF soldiers were wounded, one severely, by a roadside bomb in southern Lebanon overnight. The Home Front Command extended defense directives until Tuesday, 19 May 2026, 20:00. The law allowing the death penalty for terrorists in Judea and Samaria was signed. Ten Israeli civilians from the "Bashan Pioneers" group illegally crossed into Syria, were apprehended by IDF troops, and handed over to police. Reports from the New York Times (via @asafroz, @amitsegal, @yediotnews25) claim Israel secretly operated at least two military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, one used during the "June 2025 war with Iran," with the US allegedly compelling Iraq to shut down its radar systems to protect American aircraft. Haaretz (via @asafroz, @amitsegal, @yediotnews25) reported the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued five new secret arrest warrants for Israeli officials (three politicians, two military), in addition to existing warrants for Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Gallant, though the ICC officially denied new warrants. A fire, reportedly due to an electrical short circuit, broke out at a military base in the Negev, causing minor infrastructure damage with no casualties.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF killed Bahaa Baroud, a commander in Hamas's operations division, in Gaza, stating he posed an "immediate threat" and advanced numerous terror attacks. Two additional armed terror operatives were eliminated by IAF strikes in central and southern Gaza. Hamas condemned Israel's plan to convert the UNRWA compound in occupied Al-Quds into military facilities. The UN Special Rapporteur on Palestine, Francesca Albanese, stated Israel systematically uses torture against Palestinian detainees. Israeli settlers ran over a Palestinian farmer's sheep in the al-Tawil area of Aqraba, south of Nablus. The law allowing the death penalty for terrorists was extended to Judea and Samaria.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched multiple rockets, explosive drones, and mortar shells at IDF forces in southern Lebanon, with some projectiles falling near forces without causing injuries. The IDF intercepted several rockets fired by Hezbollah. Four IDF soldiers were wounded, one seriously, by a roadside bomb in southern Lebanon overnight. Israeli Air Force (IAF) strikes were reported in Sultaniyah, Tirelsih, Maaroub, and Souhmor in southern Lebanon. The IDF issued evacuation warnings for five villages in Lebanon: Souhmor, Roumine, Al-Qasiba, Kfar Houna, and Banafour. Hezbollah characterized Lebanon-Israel talks as a "dead end" due to continued Israeli strikes.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Ten Israeli civilians illegally crossed into Syrian territory and were detained by the IDF. The New York Times reported that Israel operated at least two secret military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, one of which was used during the "June 2025 war with Iran," with US forces reportedly compelling Iraq to shut down its radar systems to conceal the Israeli presence. An Iraqi farmer was reportedly killed after discovering a secret base. Saudi Arabia reported intercepting three drones launched from Iraq. An Israeli incursion of three tanks and a Dushka machine gun was reported in Daraa, southern Syria, with firing on passersby. An indictment in the US against Muhammad Baqer Al-Saadi, a senior Kata'ib Hezbollah official in Iraq, links him to a Molotov cocktail incident at a synagogue in Belgium and an attempted bank attack in Paris.

GULF STATES
The UAE reported a drone attack on the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the Al Dhafra region, causing a fire in an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter, with no reported casualties or impact on radiological safety. The UAE Ministry of Defense stated three drones entered from its "western borders," two were intercepted, and one hit the generator. The UAE condemned the attack as a "dangerous escalation" and an "unacceptable provocation," with its Foreign Minister discussing the incident with the IAEA Director-General, asserting the UAE's "full right to respond." Saudi Arabia announced the interception of three drones launched from Iraq, stating it reserves the right to respond. US-backed shipping giants CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd suspended all movements to and from Cuba under US orders, which sources say could jeopardize up to 60% of Cuba's shipping volume. Experts warned that damage to vital undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz could disrupt multi-continental banking, stock exchanges, energy operations, and communication networks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Imminent Military Action against Iran:** US President Trump explicitly threatened Iran with severe military action if an updated deal is not reached quickly, with a national security meeting scheduled for Tuesday to discuss options, following coordination with Israeli PM Netanyahu.
2.  **Drone Attack on UAE Nuclear Plant:** Three drones, reportedly from the "western border," targeted the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the UAE, with one hitting an electrical generator, causing a fire but no casualties or radiation leakage.
3.  **Israeli Bases in Iraq:** The New York Times reported that Israel has secretly operated at least two military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, with one used during the "June 2025 war with Iran," and the US allegedly forcing Iraq to disable its radar systems.
4.  **IDF Casualties in Southern Lebanon:** Four Israeli soldiers, including one in serious condition, were wounded by a roadside bomb in southern Lebanon overnight, indicating escalating risks for ground forces.
5.  **Houthi Downing of US Drone:** Houthi forces claimed to have shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone in Marib province, Yemen, continuing a trend of successful drone interceptions against US assets.
6.  **Iranian Threats to Strait of Hormuz:** Senior Iranian officials, including Mohsen Rezaei and Vice President Aref, reiterated threats to close the Strait of Hormuz for military passage and attack regional oil facilities if Iran's energy infrastructure is targeted.
7.  **Saudi Drone Interceptions from Iraq:** Saudi Arabia announced the interception of three drones launched from Iraq, warning of a right to respond, indicating a potential widening of the regional conflict.
8.  **IDF Manpower Crisis:** The IDF reported a critical shortage of approximately 12,000 mandatory service soldiers, including 6,000-7,500 combat personnel, citing "deep erosion" across seven simultaneous operational fronts.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of widespread escalation in the Middle East is critically high. President Trump's explicit threats and upcoming discussions on military options, coupled with ongoing US-Israeli coordination, indicate an increased likelihood of renewed hostilities against Iran. The drone attack on the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, regardless of its exact origin, signifies a dangerous expansion of target sets in the region. The continued activity of Iranian proxies, particularly the Houthis (MQ-9 downing) and Iraqi militias (drones to Saudi, alleged involvement in European terror plots), contributes to regional instability. The Israel-Lebanon border remains a flashpoint, with IDF casualties from a roadside bomb underscoring the lethal nature of cross-border engagements. Iran's threats to the Strait of Hormuz and regional oil infrastructure represent a clear red line with global economic implications if crossed. The alleged Israeli bases in Iraq add another layer of complexity and potential flashpoints, particularly given US knowledge and alleged complicity in radar shutdowns.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump issued strong threats against Iran, stating "time is running out" and he expects an updated proposal, or Iran "will be hit hard." He is scheduled to hold a Situation Room meeting on Tuesday to discuss military options. Trump also spoke with Israeli PM Netanyahu regarding Iran and discussed the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his recent trip.
**Gulf States:** The UAE condemned the drone attack on its nuclear power plant, reserving the right to respond, and its FM discussed the incident with the IAEA Director-General. Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones from Iraq and stated it reserves the right to retaliate.
**Pakistan:** Foreign Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf and Iranian FM Iraqchi in Tehran. Sources suggest Pakistan is actively mediating between Iran and the US, attempting to integrate their proposals and lower their demands. Naqvi also discussed regional developments with Egypt's Foreign Minister.
**China:** President Xi Jinping discussed the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program with US President Trump. Iran appointed Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf as a special envoy for China, signaling diplomatic efforts.
**Russia:** The Russian Defense Ministry claimed to have downed 1,054 Ukrainian drones in the last 24 hours. Putin is scheduled to visit China on Tuesday. Russia's permanent representative to international organizations, Ulyanov, warned that US and Israel might resume military action against Iran in "days, if not hours."
**Turkey:** The Turkish cabinet is scheduled to discuss the status of indirect US-Iran negotiations and the economic impact of the Strait of Hormuz blockade.
**Cuba:** Axios reported that Cuba has acquired over 300 drones from Russia and Iran and is reportedly discussing plans to attack US naval ships and Guantanamo Bay.
**Brazil:** President Lula da Silva reportedly told the Washington Post that he opposes the war in Iran.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
*   **ICC Arrest Warrants:** There is a contradiction regarding new International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrants. Haaretz and Press TV reported that five new "secret" arrest warrants were issued for Israeli politicians and military officials. However, the ICC officially denied that any new arrest warrants related to Israel have been issued, indicating either a premature leak, misinformation, or a misinterpretation of a request for warrants.
*   **Source of UAE Drone Attack:** While the UAE stated three drones originated from its "western border," an Israeli source (Channel 15) explicitly noted uncertainty about whether the perpetrators were Iranian or Houthi, indicating a lack of definitive attribution.
*   **Iraqi Radar Shutdown:** The New York Times report regarding the US forcing Iraq to shut down its radar systems during past confrontations with Iran to protect "American aircraft" raises questions about US complicity and knowledge of alleged Israeli military operations within Iraq, as Iraqi officials claimed they were not aware these were Israeli bases, only that they were "not American."
*   **"June 2025 War with Iran":** Multiple sources, including the New York Times and Israeli media, refer to a "June 2025 war with Iran" as a past event. This implies a significant past military engagement between Israel/US and Iran that is being used as a reference point for current strategic planning and past operational uses of alleged Israeli bases in Iraq.
*   **Iranian Internal Economic Situation:** A message from "mamlkete" reports that a typically busy coffee shop in Tehran is now "absolutely empty" due to a lack of money among customers, citing the owner, who stated, "nobody is here, there is no money." This provides an anecdotal but significant indicator of the economic hardship faced by ordinary Iranians, potentially exacerbated by the ongoing conflict and sanctions.
*   **Propaganda Indicators:** Statements from omid dana (e.g., claims of Khamenei's death, "layers of the regime will be stripped away," "death smells from this picture") are highly opinionated, triumphalist, and likely propagandistic in nature, reflecting a pro-opposition viewpoint rather than verified intelligence. Similarly, some statements from Press TV and SharghDaily (e.g., "Empire in freefall," "US nightmare comes true," "US-Israeli war against Iran driven by corporate profit") exhibit strong anti-Western and anti-Israeli bias, indicating a clear propaganda intent.
